reasoning: Gates fail on two axes: kelvin_ok=false (cable-1 both HI/LO unrouted; cable-2 HI unrouted) and structural DRC=20. diffpair_ok=true is the only clean gate. Three issues of note: (1) KELVIN_UNROUTED UNDERCOUNT confirmed again — failing_reasons names unconnected ratlines on /SENSEC1_HI, /SENSEC1_LO, AND /SENSEC2_HI, meaning kelvin_pairs_failing=2 (cables 1 AND 2 each have at least one Kelvin net failing) while the reported kelvin_unrouted=1. Rule 16 mandates substituting kelvin_pairs_failing=2 in all rule logic, but the scorer's objective still uses raw kelvin_unrouted=1, so the objective underpenalizes this round by ~1000 cost units (the weight for one missing cable). (2) UNCONNECTED_COUNT_MISMATCH — unconnected=4 but only 3 Kelvin-net ratlines are named in failing_reasons, leaving 1 unidentified ratline. Rule 2 mandates a full per-net unconnected retrieval and injection of the unnamed net into kelvin_stub_priority before next dispatch. (3) MULTI-CABLE KELVIN SIMULTANEOUS FAILURE — this is the first round where two distinct cable indices (1 and 2) each contribute failing Kelvin nets in the same scored round. The existing per-cable rules (Rule 14 five-consecutive stall; Rule 15 three-consecutive isolation) each track cables independently and are triggered one cable at a time. Neither rule fires a multi-cable isolation diagnostic when global routing congestion is stranding Kelvin pairs on multiple cables simultaneously. Rule 15 isolation for cable 1 alone cannot reveal whether cable 2's HI failure is caused by competition with cable 1's stubs or is an independent geometric constraint. The gap: there is no rule that recognises the multi-cable condition as a distinct congestion signal and dispatches a joint isolation round covering all currently-failing cable pairs at once. Raising kelvin_unrouted scorer weight from 1000 to 2000 partially compensates for the systematic undercount (raw score of 1 at weight 2000 approximates the true cost of 2 pairs at weight 1000), making future multi-cable rounds cost more in the objective and pushing the optimizer harder on Kelvin convergence even when the metric undercounts.

scorer_penalty.rationale: The kelvin_unrouted metric is systematically undercounted: this round reports 1 but kelvin_pairs_failing=2 (cables 1 and 2 both have failing Kelvin nets per failing_reasons). Rule 16 corrects the count in rule-evaluation logic but the scorer objective still multiplies the raw reported value. Raising weight from 1000 to 2000 means a round with true two-cable failure but reported kelvin_unrouted=1 incurs objective cost 2000 (≈1000×2), better reflecting the real routing debt. This also increases pressure on single-cable failures, which is acceptable given cable 1 has persisted across many rounds.

manager_rule: When kelvin_pairs_failing (computed per Rule 16) is >= 2 in a single scored round — meaning at least two distinct cable indices N each have one or more of /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO appearing in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines' — the manager MUST immediately dispatch a 'multi-cable Kelvin isolation round' before advancing the per-cable consecutive-failure counters for Rules 14 and 15. The isolation round stub set MUST contain stubs for ALL failing /SENSEC{N}_HI and /SENSEC{N}_LO nets across every failing cable index N, and ZERO non-Kelvin candidates (no /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA, or any other control or signal net). This fires on the basis of the multi-cable condition alone, independently of and without waiting for Rule 15's per-cable 3-consecutive threshold. The isolation round counts toward each cable's individual consecutive-failure counter for Rules 14 and 15. After the isolation round is scored: (a) if all Kelvin nets across all failing cables successfully route (none appear in failing_reasons), log 'multi_cable_kelvin_isolation_success' and resume normal stub composition on the following round; (b) if one or more cables still fail, immediately halt all FR dispatch under the same protocol as Rule 15's kelvin_isolation_fail, with the halt payload identifying by cable index which pairs cleared and which did not, the stub coordinates used for each failing pair, and the full per-net unconnected list from the isolation round's scoring artifacts. Human clearance requires: (1) revised floorplan or keepout modification opening viable routing channels for every still-failing cable's Kelvin pair, verified by showing their pad coordinates lie in a gap in the keepout map, and (2) explicit written authorization to resume. This rule is subordinate to Rules 8, 11, and 14: if any of those halt conditions fired and was not cleared before this round, the multi-cable isolation round is not dispatched and the existing halt takes precedence.
